Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one redesigned stage-magician desktop-pet action.
The attached approved Gemini magician sprite is the character model for identity, art technique, costume and compact proportions. Create the NEW stage action described below from that model. Keep her familiar charming face and short rounded body.

ART AND IDENTITY: controlled dark-violet linework with subtle thickness variation, finer facial and interior hair lines, softly colored cel shadows and irregular glossy highlights, matching the approved sprite. Voluminous wavy blue-violet hair fading to pink-magenta, curled ahoge, two side buns, fluffy blue-violet cat ears with pink and white interiors, and ONE fluffy cat tail. Pink-magenta iris on viewer's LEFT, amber-gold on viewer's RIGHT; dark pupils and small crisp highlights. The single large gold-rimmed iridescent four-pointed star hairclip and its dangling charms remain on viewer's RIGHT above the amber eye. Keep the small navy/gold tilted top hat, star collar clasp and gold-edged navy bow, white short puff sleeves, gold-edged navy waistcoat with three gold buttons, short white gloves and gold cuffs, navy star-trimmed pleated skirt over white ruffles, white leg warmers, navy-violet buckled platform shoes and short navy cape with gold edging and star-speckled violet lining. Her TWO gloves are normal softly drawn human hands.

DESIGN PRIORITY: a petite, graceful stage magician performing ONE easily readable trick. Each action has one small prop group at or below chest level, with generous open space around her face. Props remain secondary to her face and silhouette. Keep the front of the waistcoat and skirt visible. The pose has a natural little weight shift, softly bent SHORT elbows and gentle head inclination, never a rigid display of objects. The cape follows the body in a restrained small curve; tail is a relaxed expressive cat tail, not an extra prop rack. Hair and tail keep their approved volume, not enlarged to fill the frame.

FACIAL ACTING: preserve the approved cheek and chin shapes, eye-to-face ratio and natural eyelids. Let both pupils focus coherently on the named target. Use subtle eyebrow asymmetry, tiny mouth changes, cheeks and a slight head angle to convey feeling. No warped face, stretched mouth, cross-eyed gaze, huge bulging eyes, angry exaggerated brows or caricature grimace. Do not replace every expression with the neutral idle face. The exact face acting is in ACTION.

FORMAT: square, at least 1024x1024, actual transparent background. ONE full-body character. Whole figure about 90% of the image height; keep at least 40 transparent pixels above the ahoge and around ordinary side edges, and some space below the shoes. Original head/body proportions and consistent size. Entire props inside canvas. No floor, shadow, glow, frame, captions or watermark. Tangible stage-magic props only: no spell circles, floating stars, sparkles, motion strokes, effect clouds or magical beams. Tail stays free of cloth, electronics or other props. All other props are put away, including the wand unless explicitly requested. Keep her costume unchanged; only the named pose may take off the single existing hat.

SAFE FRAMING OVERRIDE: The source is almost edge-to-edge. Reframe the new sprite with MORE transparent canvas, rather than copying that placement. On a 1254-pixel square, put the very highest ahoge point around y=65 and the lowest sole around y=1190. The entire top 50-pixel horizontal band MUST be completely empty and transparent, no hair pixel or colored speck. Preserve the head-to-body proportions while fitting the complete figure inside these bounds. This framing instruction takes priority over the source pixel placement. Do not let any part of the ahoge touch the top edge.

actions.searching: SINGLE TRICK: inspecting an empty top hat before a reveal. She has removed her ONE existing little top hat; her head has no second hat. Both ears, ahoge and the rest of her hair stay complete. Hold that small hat just below the collar, tilted so a little of its dark interior is visible. Hat brim no wider than HALF her face. Glove on viewer's right supports the brim from below; the other glove slips fingertips into the opening to feel for a hidden object. Her torso leans forward only a little, head inclined toward the opening. Both pupils look DOWN into the hat, eyebrows gently arched with one a little higher, small closed inquisitive cat smile, softly lifted cheeks. Curious and clever, like she is checking her secret hiding place. Shoulders relaxed, feet standing compactly, tail curls lightly on viewer's right. The hat is the ONLY prop. No silk, flowers, wand or animal.
actions.asking: SINGLE TRICK: an intimate 'pick a card' invitation. Her little top hat stays worn. At lower-chest level, the glove on viewer's left holds a SMALL fan of just THREE overlapping face-down cards; the other glove gently offers the outermost card toward the viewer, still overlapping the fan, so the two hands form one little stage gesture. Cards are small, one card about the length of her glove, the whole fan narrower than HALF her face. Navy backs, thin gold edges and one simple four-pointed star, no text/numbers/suits. Head tilted gently toward the offered card but both eyes meet the VIEWER. One soft eyebrow a little raised, a tiny asymmetric closed cat smile, warmly expectant and playfully confident. One small foot slightly forward, relaxed short elbows; cape falls behind her, tail curls softly. No wand, rings, cloth or extra objects. Keep cards well below the chin.
actions.happy: SINGLE TRICK: reveal ONE small white flower from behind her cape with a graceful stage flourish. Little top hat stays worn. One gloved hand presents a single delicate five-petal white stage flower, with a short navy-violet stem and pale gold center, at upper-waist height on viewer's left. Flower head no wider than her glove, stem only a glove-length; no bouquet or leaves filling the face area. Her OTHER glove gently pinches the gold-edged near corner of her cape on viewer's right and draws it sideways by only a glove-width, as if she has just uncovered the little flower from behind it. Short elbow softly bent, small graceful reveal, not a wide cape-spreading pose. Keep the white puff sleeve and front of her waistcoat visible. Body faces the viewer, one foot tucked a little beside the other, head gives a tiny pleased tilt. BOTH eyes OPEN with naturally curved lids and coherent warm eye contact with viewer, eyebrows softly lifted asymmetrically, gently lifted cheeks, a tiny closed happy cat smile with one corner a little higher. This is her clever little successful reveal, not loud laughing or a victory fist pose. Tail curls happily and cape makes one restrained outward fold. No wand, cards, rings or cloth.
actions.compact: SINGLE TRICK: neatly squaring a card fan back into a tiny deck after a performance. Little top hat stays on her head. Just below the collar, both gloved hands gently gather THREE small overlapping navy-backed cards into ONE tidy compact packet: the glove on viewer's right supports the little deck, the other presses its protruding top card flush. The entire packet is about one glove-length, much narrower than her face. Navy backs, thin gold edges and a small four-pointed star, no letters, numbers or suit symbols. Head slightly bowed toward the hands, both pupils look DOWN at the card edges, natural curved lids relaxed, one brow gently lowered in careful concentration, a tiny satisfied closed cat smile, cheeks softly relaxed. Shoulders and elbows remain soft, two feet planted together; tail rests in a little curl. No suitcase, loose papers, removed hat, silk, rings, wand or straining grimace.
actions.busy_left: SINGLE TRICK: gently linking TWO SMALL gold magician rings with her hands. Her torso and shoulders angle shallowly toward viewer's LEFT; still see both eyes. Each glove holds ONE thin smooth gold ring at mid-chest on viewer's left. The rings touch and interlock once, making ONE compact prop group; each ring's diameter about one glove-width, and both together no wider than HALF her face. No third ring. Fingers gently curl around ring edges; both elbows naturally bent close to her body, never reaching stiffly straight out. Head bows and tilts toward their point of contact; BOTH pupils look DOWN and LEFT at the joining point. Calm lively concentration: relaxed gracefully arched eyebrows with slight asymmetry, tiny knowing closed cat smile, softly lifted cheeks, no angry frown. Little hat stays on head, cape curves softly behind, tail curls freely on viewer's right. Feet compact, small natural weight shift. The TWO rings are the ONLY props. No wand, cards, silk, electronics or cable.
actions.swamped_left: SINGLE TRICK: a small card flourish almost slips, and she catches it. Body inclines gently toward viewer's LEFT, both short legs remain compact and one heel is lifted only slightly. At chest height on viewer's LEFT, TWO gloved hands catch a little crooked group of THREE navy-backed cards: one glove holds two overlapping cards, the other catches the third by a corner, still touching the packet. This is ONE small connected prop group, no cards scattered across the canvas. Each card is about one glove-length; the entire group narrower than HALF her face, well below chin level. Navy backs with thin gold trim and one four-pointed star, no letters, numbers or suits. Both pupils look DOWN and LEFT at the slipping card, comfortably open eyes with normal-size irises, eyebrows lift gently and unevenly, mouth makes a tiny softly parted 'oh' shape, not stretched or zigzagged. A sweet believable moment of fluster, no distorted face. Ears lean back slightly; tail lifts a little while keeping normal fluffy size. Hat remains on. NO rings, silk, wand, electronics, pencil, sweat icons or floating effects.
actions.busy_right: Create the RIGHT-facing companion of image 1's new small TWO-ring trick. Use image 1 for the tiny two-ring prop group and hand choreography; image 2 is the approved design for facial identity and asymmetric ornaments. Turn torso and shoulders shallowly toward viewer's RIGHT, both eyes still visible. Hands and their two little interlinked rings now work at mid-chest on viewer's RIGHT; each ring diameter one glove-width, the entire group smaller than HALF her face. Both short elbows stay softly bent. Head inclines toward the joining point; both pupils look DOWN and RIGHT at it, soft asymmetric brows and a tiny calm clever cat smile. Tail curls freely on viewer's LEFT and cape follows gently, same compact body and feet. The TWO small rings are the only props. No wand, cloth, cards, electronics or third ring. IMPORTANT: redraw the opposite direction without mirroring the face: pink eye stays viewer's LEFT, gold eye viewer's RIGHT, and the large star hairclip stays visibly on viewer's RIGHT above the amber eye. Keep the normal delicate facial contours and small worn hat.
actions.swamped_right: Create the RIGHT-facing companion of image 1's small near-failed card flourish. Image 1 defines the same small THREE-card group and gentle catch; image 2 defines original face and asymmetries. Gently incline body toward viewer's RIGHT. Both gloved hands catch the little crooked packet at chest height on viewer's RIGHT: two overlapping small cards supported by one glove, the third caught at its corner by the other glove and touching the packet. The cards are one glove-length, the entire group smaller than HALF her face and below chin. Both pupils look DOWN and RIGHT at the third card, natural open eyes with normal-size irises, gently lifted uneven eyebrows, tiny softly parted 'oh' mouth. Sweet slightly flustered face; no bulging eyes, stretched or wavy grimace. Hat stays worn, normal fluffy tail lifts lightly on viewer's LEFT, cape follows softly, short body and legs remain compact. Cards are the ONLY props; no rings, cloth, wand, electronics, pencil, sweat icons or effects. IMPORTANT: do not mirror the face ornaments: pink eye stays viewer's LEFT, amber eye viewer's RIGHT, the large star clip stays viewer's RIGHT above the amber eye.
